item.description:
Senate edges closer to vote on Israeli accountability for US citizens killed in West Bank, Democrat says

Submitted by Yasmine El-Sabawi on Thu, 09/24/2026 - 20:40
Nine US citizens have been killed by Israelis in the occupied West Bank over the last four years
US Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) speaks during a forum on President Donald Trump's crypto dealings, co-hosted by Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) in the Dirksen Senate Office in Washington, DC, on 27 July 2026 (Finn Gomez/Getty Images/AFP)
Off

Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen said on Thursday that a vote on holding Israel accountable for the killings of nine US citizens in the occupied West Bank, as well as the imprisonment of three others, could take place as soon as next week.

Van Hollen, a vocal supporter of Palestinian rights and curbing US aid to Israel, introduced Senate Resolution 852 earlier this month, pursuant to Section 502(b) of the Foreign Assistance Act, which allows lawmakers to request human rights reports from the State Department on countries that receive US assistance. 

Israel is the largest recipient of US foreign aid, with $3.3bn received in 2025. 

Speaking to the IMEU Policy Project in a virtual session on Thursday, Van Hollen said he was optimistic given that 24 Democratic senators are already on board.

"These are Democratic senators who have put their names on the resolution, which is definitely progress from where we were two years ago when fighting for human rights for Palestinians, whether in Gaza or the West Bank, [it] was a lonely effort," he said. 

"This vote is likely to come up early next week. It's what's called a privileged resolution, meaning that after a certain amount of time elapses from its introduction, it can be brought up for a vote," he noted. 

Privileged resolutions can bypass other business because they command urgency in the interest of accountability for the American public. 

If the vote does not take place next week, it will have to wait until after the 3 November midterm elections, Van Hollen said.

He urged Americans to ramp up their calls and emails to their senators in the coming days. 

"We're at a moment where we see growing recognition throughout the public that is slowly filtering up and slowly having an impact on the bubble that is the United States Congress, and so I think that this is a moment where we can use the fact that American citizens are not getting accountability and justice to shine the light on the fact that Palestinian children and others in the West Bank are subjected to these kinds of abuses every single day," Van Hollen told the IMEU Policy Project.

The key obstacle to his resolution, he added, is that "not a single Republican senator is willing to stand up and demand justice for these American citizens". 

The 100-member Senate is currently made up of 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats.

In a tied result, Republican Vice President JD Vance would cast the tie-breaking vote. 

Letter to Netanyahu

Last month, 45 Senate Democrats signed a letter addressed to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, urging his "personal and direct engagement and intervention in order to protect our constituents and their families". 

"The last few weeks alone saw a significant surge in violence on both sides, resulting in a large-scale response by Israeli security forces, mass arrests of Palestinians, and reported attacks by settlers on mosques,” the senators wrote of the occupied West Bank.

“We urge you to take measures to prevent and intercede in this violence, establish a credible mechanism to investigate violations of law, and to make clear that the Government of Israel will not tolerate violence by its people, just as it does not tolerate violence against its people," the letter added. 

The senators called for Israel to complete its own investigations into the deaths of the nine US citizens. 

Many of them became high-profile cases, yet Washington never demanded independent investigations outside of the Israeli military's purview.

Al Jazeera journalist Shireen Abu Akleh appeared to have been targeted by Israeli forces in 2022 when she was shot in the head. Activist Ayşenur Ezgi Eygi was killed by Israeli forces during a protest against the building of illegal settlements near Nablus in 2024. item.description:
Netanyahu paints Israel's critics as 'antisemites' in angry UN speech to near-empty hall

Submitted by Sean Mathews on Thu, 09/24/2026 - 21:15
Israeli leader attacks everyone from New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani to Turkey's Erdogan and France in his address
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks at the United Nations General Assembly in New York City, on 24 September 2026 (Alexi J Rosenfeld/Getty Images/AFP)
Off

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave a pugnacious speech at the United Nations General Assembly, attacking everyone from New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and the leaders of Western Europe, as he tried to counter Israel’s growing international isolation.

Netanyahu did not hold back from taking an aggressive stance towards critics when the General Assembly hall erupted in boos as he took to the podium, with most delegates walking out in protest.

“Order in the hall, please. Order in the hall, please,” the president of the General Assembly could be heard shouting, trying to silence the room.

“If there are any other moral cowards who haven’t left this hall, please do so now,” Netanyahu said, smiling, before he began his speech.

Israel is locked in conflict with many of its neighbours - including Lebanon and Syria - even as it continues attacking the Gaza Strip and the occupied West Bank. While Netanyahu addressed foreign policy, he spent a big chunk of his time attacking Mamdani, who he accused of succumbing to “antisemitic mobs”.

“Mr Mamdani, since you were elected mayor of this city, many Jews no longer feel safe in New York,” Netanyahu shouted. “Mr Mamdani, you tried to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth,” he said.

Meanwhile, hundreds of protesters took up positions around the UN headquarters before his arrival and continued protesting while Netanyahu spoke inside. 

Netanyahu’s remarks are a reminder of how much he geared his address to an American audience and also sought to play up politics within the diaspora ahead of Israel’s October elections. 

'Easiest decision I made'

The Israeli leader claimed the US-Israeli war on Iran as a victory, saying he was proud to have attacked “Iran’s murderous dictatorship” alongside the US.

“Devastating Iran’s nuclear facilities was hard. It was very hard to do. But for me, it was one of the easiest decisions I’ve ever had to make as prime minister,” he said.

“I vowed to prevent Iran's murderous dictatorship from developing atomic bombs, nuclear weapons aimed at destroying Israel, nuclear weapons that could threaten the entire world," he said.

Netanyahu held up a Starlink satellite internet receiver during his speech, saying that he would leave it for Iran’s delegation. The US and Israel are believed to have tried to provide Iranian dissidents with Starlink to communicate during anti-government riots at the start of this year.

"So when they inevitably defect, they too will be able to freely tell their story on social media," he said.

The US-Israeli war on Iran has not toppled the Islamic Republic. Iran has moved to demonstrate its control over the Strait of Hormuz, while in Yemen, Iran’s allies, the Houthis, have taken the territory on the Arabian Gulf side of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Netanyahu condemned the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel, where around 1,200 people were killed, calling it the darkest day in Israel's history. He repeated accusations about the attack that investigators and academics have long debunked, along with Israeli eyewitnesses.

Accusing Western Europe of hypocrisy

“They slaughtered Holocaust survivors, they burned babies alive in front of their parents. They beheaded our men, they brutally raped our women, and then they murdered them,” he said.

Israel conducted a ferocious onslaught on Gaza in response to 7 October that has killed close to 74,000 Palestinians and wounded nearly 175,000. The United Nations and dozens of human rights groups have called Israel’s war a genocide. The International Criminal Court (ICC) has issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant.

Netanyahu said Israel was engaged in a “seven-front war”, with its soldiers fighting like “lions”.

“Israel is defending many of the countries whose delegates just left this hall. Many of their leaders even thank us privately for taking out Iran’s nukes,” he said.

In reality, Israel has faced growing international isolation. Netanyahu took aim at European countries that have declared trade sanctions on the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

He attacked Britain and France for their past colonial empires, accusing them of hypocrisy for criticising Israel.

"They accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism - some colonialism. And who's accusing us? Among them are people in Britain and in France. For God's sake, they invented the term," he said.

Netanyahu launched a tirade against several countries in the Middle East and said Israel faced an “eight-front” war combating media coverage critical of his country.

Lashing out at Turkey, Qatar and Syria

He lashed out at the president of Syria, Ahmed al-Sharaa, who earlier this week condemned Israel’s occupation of the Golan Heights.

“Mr al-Sharaa, you should know that Jews have been on the Golan Heights since the days of Moses,” he said.

Netanyahu also attacked Qatar and Al Jazeera. He said that Turkey was a “super-spreader of antisemitic lies” and called his counterpart, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, “a tyrant”.

The only world leader Netanyahu singled out for praise was US President Donald Trump.

“We have no greater partner than President Trump. I thank him,” he said.

Netanyahu also dismissed the rising Israeli settler attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. Earlier this week, Jordanian King Abdullah II said Israel was undertaking de facto annexation of the territory and was guilty of war crimes there.

He said “a handful of young juvenile delinquents, about 150 in number, who throw stones, who chop down olive trees” were causing unrest in the occupied territory.

Mohamud also said that “a just resolution to the Palestinian question remains essential to lasting peace in the Middle East and beyond”.

“Somalia stands firmly with the Palestinian people and their legitimate right to self-determination and statehood.”

European Union: 'We need multilateralism'

Antonio Costa, president of the European Union Council, began his speech to the General Assembly by defending “multilateralism”.

“Alone no country… can build lasting peace. This is why our message is clear. We need multilateralism,” he said. 

Costa did not name the US’s attacks on the International Criminal Court (ICC) directly, but he warned over “double standards in international law” and said the European Union would defend the ICC and the International Court of Justice (ICJ).

EU foreign policy chief says Israeli settlements should be treated like Russian-occupied Crimea
Read More »

“We support these courts firmly, and we will defend their independence, integrity and ability to fully carry out their mandate,” he said, condemning “attacks” on the ICC.

Washington has already imposed sanctions on several top ICC officials, including court president Tomoko Akane, who was sanctioned in August along with senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye.

Former chief prosecutor Karim Khan was the first to be sanctioned in February last year, followed by two deputy prosecutors and nine judges involved in the court’s Palestine and Afghanistan investigations. 

The Wall Street Journal reported this week that the US is planning new sweeping sanctions on the court.

Costa also took an indirect jab at Trump’s claim to have brought a peaceful resolution to Israel’s genocide in Gaza. Israeli attacks on the enclave are continuing despite a ceasefire sealed in 2025.

“We regret the current stalemate in Gaza, and more broadly speaking in Palestine,” Costa said.

“The EU and its member states have made their position clear. The two-state solution is the only one that can secure lasting peace in the Middle East,” he added.

Costa did not criticise the US-Israeli war on Iran. Instead, he said the EU supports efforts to “find a solution to the conflict". 

“It is essential that Iran never be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons,” he said. “We hope the Iranian people can live in peace, security and as free men and women,” he added.

“Freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz must be preserved without conditions and without hindrance,” he said.

Yemen ties its stability to Red Sea navigation

Vice President of Yemen Abdullah Abdulkader al-Alimi-Bawzer condemned the Houthis in his address to the UN General Assembly and tried to rally the global community to help fight the group.

Saudi war against Houthis displaces 130,000 Yemenis as hunger crisis deepens
Read More »

“The people of Yemen, this great nation… [have] been enduring for 12 years the consequences of the coup carried out by the terrorist Houthi militia,” he said.

He said the government of Yemen had supported a peace initiative backed by the governments of Saudi Arabia and Oman, while the Houthis rejected it and “instead escalated their actions in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb to serve an Iranian agenda”.

“Turning one of the world’s most important waterways into a tool of pressure and bargaining in Iran’s confrontation with the world,” he said.

He called for “decisive action” to degrade the Houthis and praised Saudi Arabia’s support for the internationally recognised government of Yemen.

“The Houthi militia’s use of the safety of navigation as a tool for blackmail threatens not only Yemen. It is taking hostage the entire global economy,” he said.

“Maritime security in the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb and the Gulf of Aden can’t be built while a non-state armed militia remains on the shores,” he said.

“Restoring the Yemeni state and restoring the security of Bab al-Mandeb are inseparable,” he said.

Kuwait condemns Iran attacks

Crown Prince of Kuwait Sabah Al Khaled condemned the “illegal Iranian aggression” in his address to the UN Security Council on Thursday.

“These attacks are a flagrant violation of international law,” he said. “These brutal attacks have systematically and repeatedly targeted civilian objects and critical infrastructure… revealing a hostile approach aimed at disrupting the foundations of life.”

“The security and stability of the Arabian Gulf region constitutes a fundamental pillar of regional and international security and stability, as demonstrated by the repercussions of the war and Iranian aggressions,” he said. 

Kuwait was one of the Gulf states hardest hit by Iran in retaliation for the US-Israeli war on the Islamic Republic. Kuwait is home to tens of thousands of US troops and military bases. US facilities in Kuwait were attacked along with civilian sites like Kuwait airport and energy infrastructure.

Kuwait is one of the most exposed countries to Iran’s blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, as the country uses tankers to transport nearly all of its oil exports.

"The State of Kuwait reiterates its principled and firm position condemning the ongoing violations by the Israeli occupation forces against the brotherly Palestinian people," he said. 

"The Palestinian people continue to suffer under difficult living conditions caused by policies of displacement, arrest and settlement," he added.

Kuwait also praised France and the UK for imposing sanctions on trade in goods from Israeli settlements. 

Khaled also called for Security Council “reform”, citing changes in the global balance of power. 

“There is an urgent need for the council to become more representative, effective and transparent in carrying out its responsibilities,” he said.

Israel

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave a pugnacious speech at the United Nations General Assembly, attacking everyone from New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and the leaders of Western Europe, as he tried to counter Israel’s growing international isolation.

Netanyahu did not hold back from taking an aggressive stance towards critics when the General Assembly hall erupted in boos as he took to the podium, with the majority of delegates walking out in protest.

“Order in the hall, please. Order in the hall, please,” the president of the General Assembly could be heard shouting, trying to silence the room.

“If there are any other moral cowards who haven’t left this hall, please do so now,” Netanyahu said, smiling, before he began his speech.

Israel is locked in conflict with many of its neighbours - including Lebanon and Syria - even as it continues attacking the Gaza Strip and the occupied West Bank. While Netanyahu addressed foreign policy, he spent a big chunk of his time attacking Mamdani, whom he accused of succumbing to “antisemitic mobs”.

“Mr Mamdani, since you were elected mayor of this city, many Jews no longer feel safe in New York,” Netanyahu shouted. “Mr Mamdani, you tried to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth,” he said.

Meanwhile, hundreds of protesters took up positions around the UN headquarters before his arrival and continued protesting while Netanyahu spoke inside. 

Netanyahu’s remarks are a reminder of how much he geared his address to an American audience and also sought to play up politics within the diaspora ahead of Israel’s October elections.

item.description:
Hormuz transits fall to single digits

Vessel transits at the Strait of Hormuz fell to nine on Thursday to nine, preliminary ship tracking data showed.

This shows a dip from the previous day where 14 vessels travelled in the waterway, as well as an overall decrease from the 10-day average of around 18.

According to Reuters, eight ships exited and one entered. Vessels exiting include the ballast very large gas carrier and a laden very large crude carrier (VLCC).  

Other vessels exiting include the Panamax, Supramax, short-range and medium-range tankers. Meanwhile, one dry bulk handymax carrier entered the strait.

The figures are subject to change as some vessels may be sailing through the waterways with their transponders turned off.

Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran

Colombia on Thursday announced that it formally severed diplomatic relations with Iran, citing it "deteriorated" in Tehran. 

The Foreign Ministry said the decision took effect on Saturday due to "national and hemispheric security concerns," accusing Iran of human rights violations as well as alleged links to international terrorist and narcoterrorist groups.

"Colombia also took into account confirmed human rights violations, verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities' obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran's nuclear program," the ministry said. 

"These facts deteriorated Colombia’s trust in the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran."

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Gaza suffers ‘world’s most severe economic crisis on record’, UN says
item.description:
Gaza suffers ‘world’s most severe economic crisis on record’, UN says  

Submitted by MEE staff on Fri, 09/25/2026 - 08:30
UNCTAD report says Israeli attacks have devastated Gaza’s economy, with $71.5bn needed for recovery and reconstruction
An Israeli flag flutters in Gaza, as seen from the Israeli side of the border, 23 September 2026 (Amir Cohen/Reuters)
Off

The Gaza Strip has suffered the world’s most severe economic crisis on record following three years of Israeli genocide, according to a UN report.

The report, published on Thursday by the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), said intense military operations had destroyed more than 90 percent of economic establishments  and displaced the entire Palestinian population in Gaza.

It estimated that $71.5bn would be needed for recovery and reconstruction.

“Gaza has experienced the world’s most severe economic crisis on record,” the report said.

“Once a permanent ceasefire is secured, the international community should immediately mobilize large-scale financial and technical support, to rebuild Palestinian productive capacities,” it added. 

“A viable, sovereign, independent Palestinian State, as called for in United Nations resolutions, is a precondition for regional and global peace. Yet it cannot be built on a collapsed economy.”

The report said the Palestinian economy had been systematically stunted by decades of “de-development” under Israeli occupation.

It said Israel had imposed structural constraints on it since the occupation began in 1967.

'The destruction of public and private assets and the denial of livelihoods foster a coercive environment that forces Palestinians to leave their homeland'

- UNCTAD report

But the “cost of 59 years of occupation has skyrocketed since October 2023”.

In Gaza, “unprecedented” military operations since then brought productive activity to an almost complete halt.

The three-year genocide damaged or destroyed 92 percent of economic establishments, the report said.

Gaza’s GDP per capita stood at just $212 in 2025, equivalent to around $0.58 per person per day in GDP terms.

“​​At $161 in 2024, real GDP per capita was the lowest of any economy tracked through the World Bank world development indicators; by 2025, the figure had risen only marginally, to $212,” the report said.

More than 90 percent of working-age Palestinians in Gaza are now unemployed, pushing the population into “multidimensional poverty”.

The housing sector suffered the greatest damage and losses, with Israeli forces destroying or damaging nearly 90 percent of homes in the Strip.

The agricultural sector has collapsed, while the health system has been effectively destroyed, the report said.

Meanwhile, virtually all educational facilities have been damaged or destroyed, leaving 93 percent in need of reconstruction.

West Bank fragmented into ‘disconnected islands’

The UN report said the “unprecedented” destruction in Gaza had spilled over into the occupied West Bank.

It said Israel was “fragmenting the West Bank into disconnected islands”, while settlement expansion was accelerating amid a “notable shift towards formal annexation”.
 
Israeli policies there were preventing the development of an integrated Palestinian economy, the report said.

These included increased restrictions on Palestinian movement, ongoing home demolitions and displacement, denial of access to underground water, settler attacks on olive harvests and continued settlement expansion.

'There are two distinct legal regimes in the West Bank, one for Israeli settlers and another for Palestinians'

- UNCTAD report

Unemployment in the West Bank rose sharply after 2023, from 13.1 percent in 2022 to 31.4 percent in 2024. It then fell to 28.7 percent in 2025, according to the report.

“The destruction of public and private assets and the denial of livelihoods foster a coercive environment that forces Palestinians to leave their homeland,” it said.

“This, combined with increasing settler numbers, is gradually transforming the demographic composition of the West Bank.”

The report noted that 1,697 Palestinians were displaced in the first three months of 2026, surpassing the total number displaced throughout 2025.

“There are two distinct legal regimes in the West Bank, one for Israeli settlers and another for Palestinians, offering less protection, resulting in systematic inequality in movement, access to land, livelihoods and essential services.”
